q: 按正确顺序排列 system design 面试准备的基础阶段：
q_en: Put the foundation stages for system design interview prep in the right order:
steps: 选择一个 delivery framework，作为面试当天的线性路线图
理解 system design interview 到底考什么，可先看 intro 或 mock interview
学习 core concepts、key technologies、common patterns，建立知识地图
why: 先理解面试形态，再选 delivery framework 固定推进顺序，最后补 core concepts 等知识地图；顺序错了容易只背孤立组件。
why_en: Learn the interview format first, then pick a delivery framework, and only then fill in the core-concepts knowledge map.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    A["1 Intro"] --> B["2 Delivery"]
    B --> C["3 Concepts"]
    C --> D["Practice"]
tradeoff: 先搭路线图 vs 直接刷知识点

termDefinitions.meaning: 面试时固定按顺序推进设计的答题框架，例如需求→接口→数据模型→高层设计→深潜。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A delivery framework is a fixed step-by-step structure for walking through a system design answer.

termDefinitions.meaning: 和另一人模拟真实计时面试，练习临场表达。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A mock interview is a timed practice session with another person that simulates the real interview.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统设计里可复用的基础概念，例如一致性、缓存、扩展性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Core concepts are the reusable system-design ideas such as consistency, caching, and scalability.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统设计常用的具体技术组件，例如数据库、消息队列。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Key technologies are the concrete components such as databases and message queues used in designs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统设计里反复出现的架构套路，例如读写分离、扇出。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Common patterns are recurring architecture strategies that show up across many designs.

scenario: 你从没做过 system design interview，连流程和预期都不清楚。
scenario_en: You have never done a system design interview, and you do not yet know the flow or expectations.
q: 准备的第一步最应该是什么？
q_en: What should be the first preparation step?
options: 跳过所有基础准备，直接把市面上流传的 30 套完整题解全部背下来
准备第一次面试前，先读一篇 intro 或看一次 mock interview
只闷头刷 LeetCode 算法题，完全不碰系统设计相关的内容
还没打基础就直接挑战 ChatGPT 这类公认最难的系统设计题目
options_en: Skip all the basics and memorize every one of the thirty full write-up solutions out there.
Before your first attempt, read an intro article or watch one mock interview.
Only grind LeetCode algorithm problems and skip system design content entirely.
Jump straight into notoriously hard problems like ChatGPT before building any foundation.
why: 没做过这类面试时，先建立面试形态的整体画面最重要：面试官怎么问、你怎么澄清需求、设计怎么逐步展开。
why_en: If you have never done a system design interview, learn the format and expectations before memorizing full solutions.
whenOtherWins: 如果你已经熟悉面试流程，下一步该练 delivery framework 和刻意练习，而不是重复看 intro。
tradeoff: 先摸清面试形态 vs 直接冲刺具体考题

termDefinitions.meaning: 考察如何设计大规模分布式系统的技术面试环节。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A system design interview evaluates how you design a large-scale distributed system.

termDefinitions.meaning: 和另一人模拟真实计时面试，练习临场表达。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A mock interview is a timed practice session with another person that simulates the real interview.

termDefinitions.meaning: 入门介绍文章，讲解面试形式和评分预期。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The intro is an introductory article explaining the interview format and what is expected.

optionExplanations: 跳过基础硬背题解只是复述别人的思路，遇到追问就卡壳，练不出自己的判断。
新手先看一次入门介绍或示范面试，能摸清面试官会怎么问、怎么打分，后面学习才有方向。
只刷算法练不到架构取舍和需求澄清，系统设计考的是另一套能力。
新手一上来就啃最难题，框架不熟又要扛复杂约束，两头都学不会。
optionExplanations_en: Rote-memorizing full write-ups just repeats someone else's thinking, and it stalls under any follow-up question.
A beginner should read a short intro or watch one demo interview first to see how interviewers probe and grade.
Grinding only algorithms skips architecture tradeoffs and requirements clarification, a different skill entirely.
Starting on the hardest problem stacks an unfamiliar framework on top of heavy constraints, so neither sticks.

scenario: 35 分钟的系统设计面试要覆盖需求、接口、数据模型和两轮深潜，时间是硬约束。
scenario_en: You have 35 minutes to cover requirements, API, data model, and two deep dives — time is the hard constraint.
q: 为什么准备时要选择一个 delivery framework？
q_en: Why should your prep include choosing a delivery framework?
options: 它能在快节奏面试里线性推进，避免出现 scope creep
它能完全替代掌握系统设计所需要的全部技术知识和实战经验
它能保证每一道系统设计题目都只存在唯一一个标准答案
它的用途只是写在简历上装饰一下，面试当天完全用不到
options_en: It keeps you moving linearly in a fast interview and prevents scope creep from happening.
It can completely replace all the technical knowledge and hands-on experience system design requires.
It guarantees every single system design question has exactly one standard answer.
Its only use is decorating a resume — it is completely useless on interview day.
why: 系统设计面试时间紧，框架帮你按需求→接口→数据模型→高层设计→深潜推进，没有路线图很容易来回跳。
why_en: A delivery framework gives you a linear roadmap through requirements, API, data model, and deep dives so you don't drift under time pressure.
tradeoff: 固定路线图 vs 自由发挥的即兴设计

termDefinitions.meaning: 面试时固定推进顺序的答题框架，如需求→接口→数据模型→高层设计→深潜。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A delivery framework is a fixed sequence of stages for walking through a design answer.

termDefinitions.meaning: 讨论不断扩散、偏离核心需求的现象。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Scope creep is when the discussion keeps expanding beyond the core requirements.

optionExplanations: 框架把设计拆成固定阶段推进，时间紧张时也不会来回跳步骤，这正是它存在的意义。
框架只管推进顺序，不装技术知识，光有框架撑不起深潜内容。
系统设计通常没有唯一解，框架管的是流程而不是标准答案。
框架是面试当天要用的推进工具，不是简历装饰，全程都靠它定节奏。
optionExplanations_en: A framework breaks the answer into fixed stages, so you keep moving forward instead of jumping around under time pressure.
A framework only manages sequence — it carries no technical depth, so it can't fill in the deep-dive content by itself.
System design rarely has one right diagram; the framework governs process, not a single correct answer.
The framework is a tool you use live in the interview to set pace, not something reserved for a resume.

scenario: 你零系统设计经验、距面试还有两周，想先建一层能复用到所有题的底座。
scenario_en: You have zero system design experience and two weeks left, and you want a base that carries across every question.
q: 系统设计新手先该补哪些高层基础材料？（多选）
q_en: Which high-level foundation materials should a beginner study first? (Select all that apply.)
options: Core Concepts
Key Technologies
Common Patterns
只看公司股票价格
options_en: Core Concepts
Key Technologies
Common Patterns
Only look at the company's stock price
why: core concepts、key technologies、patterns 是知识地图的骨架，练习题建立在这些可复用概念上，不用每题从零发明。
why_en: Core concepts, key technologies, and common patterns form the reusable knowledge base that practice questions build on.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    K["Knowledge map"] --> C["Core concepts"]
    K --> T["Key technologies"]
    K --> P["Common patterns"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统设计里可复用的基础概念，例如一致性、缓存、扩展性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Core Concepts are the reusable system-design ideas such as consistency, caching, and scalability.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统设计常用的具体技术组件，例如数据库、消息队列。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Key Technologies are the concrete components such as databases and message queues.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统设计里反复出现的架构套路，例如读写分离、扇出。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Common Patterns are recurring architecture strategies seen across many designs.

optionExplanations: 补了它，做题时才有一致性、缓存、扩展性这类词汇去分析取舍，不然每道题都要临时现造判断框架。
补了它，深潜时才能具体说出数据库、消息队列该怎么用，不然架构图画得出却讲不清组件。
补了它，遇到相似场景能直接套用读写分离、扇出这类套路，不用每次重新发明。
股价是商业八卦，跟判断该选什么架构没有关系，纯属浪费准备时间。
optionExplanations_en: Core Concepts give you vocabulary like consistency, caching, and scalability so you're not inventing a reasoning framework mid-question.
Key Technologies let you name concrete components like databases or queues during a deep dive instead of leaving the diagram unexplained.
Common Patterns let you reuse moves like read-write splitting or fan-out instead of reinventing them for every similar problem.
Stock price is business trivia — it has nothing to do with picking an architecture and just burns prep time.

scenario: 备考只剩三周、每天一小时，要在读讲解和自己从零画设计之间分配这一小时。
scenario_en: With three weeks left and one hour a day, you must split that hour between reading write-ups and designing from scratch yourself.
q: 备考时应该如何看待“被动看内容”和“实际动手练习”？
q_en: How should you compare passive reading with hands-on practice in system design prep?
options: 被动看内容就够，不用再练习
被动学习有用，但主动做题记得更多
只看答案 key，不用自己设计
练习只适合 senior，新手不用练
options_en: Passive reading alone is enough; no need to practice.
Passive reading helps, but active practice retains far more.
Just read the answer key; you don't need to design it yourself.
Practice is only useful for senior engineers, not beginners.
why: 被动阅读有帮助，但真正动手设计能记得更多；系统设计考的是输出能力，不只是能不能认出正确答案。
why_en: Passive reading helps, but actively designing the system yourself builds far stronger retention and interview performance.
tradeoff: 被动阅读积累认知 vs 主动输出练表达
optionExplanations: 只读不做等于把输出能力完全跳过，面试现场要自己组织设计，光读懂靠不住。
阅读能打底，但真正记得住、讲得出的部分来自自己动手设计，两者要搭配而不是二选一。
只看答案 key 会被作者的思路牵着走，暴露不出自己真正卡在哪。
新手恰恰最缺输出经验，练习正是用来提前暴露这些缺口的。
optionExplanations_en: Reading alone skips output practice entirely, and the real interview requires you to organize the design yourself.
Reading builds a base, but what actually sticks — and what you can explain live — comes from doing the design yourself, not either one alone.
Only reading the answer key means the author's reasoning carries you, so your own gaps never surface.
Beginners are exactly the ones missing output experience — practice is how those gaps get exposed early.

q: 按正确顺序排列一轮推荐的题目练习流程：
q_en: Put one recommended practice loop for a design question in the right order:
steps: 读 requirements，明确要设计什么
自己在 guided practice 或白板上先尝试完整回答
看 answer key，对比自己的设计差距
做几题后找 peer mock，在时间压力下讲出来
why: 先选题、读需求，再自己尝试完整作答，然后对照 answer key 找差距，最后做 peer mock 练时间压力下的表达。
why_en: The loop is choose a question, read the requirements, attempt it yourself, compare against the answer key, and finish with a peer mock.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    Q["Pick question"] --> R["Read reqs"]
    R --> S["Solve first"]
    S --> A["Compare answer"]
    A --> M["Peer mock"]
tradeoff: 先自己产出 vs 先看答案抄结构

termDefinitions.meaning: 官方参考题解，用来对照自己的设计差距。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An answer key is the reference solution used to compare against your own design.

termDefinitions.meaning: 和另一位工程师模拟真实计时面试。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A peer mock is a timed practice interview run with another engineer.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分步骤引导、边做边给反馈的练习工具。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Guided practice is a step-by-step exercise tool that gives feedback as you design.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用来画架构图的绘图工具或表面，比如 Excalidraw。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A whiteboard is a drawing surface, such as Excalidraw, used to sketch the architecture.

scenario: 你刚选了一道 Bitly 题，还没有尝试自己设计，就很想直接看完整题解。
scenario_en: You just picked a Bitly design question and want to read the full solution before trying it yourself.
q: 看完整题解前应该怎么做？
q_en: What should you do before reading the answer key?
options: 直接背下 answer key 的内容
先按需求设计一版，再看 answer key
先读一半 answer key，再接着往下设计
先看架构图，再照着抄一遍设计
options_en: Just memorize the answer key directly.
Design your own version first, then read the answer key.
Read half the answer key, then design the rest yourself.
Look at the diagram first, then copy the design from it.
why: 先自己尝试才会暴露真实缺口：需求漏项、接口不清、深潜没展开；直接看答案容易产生“我懂了”的错觉。
why_en: Trying the design yourself first exposes real gaps that reading the answer key directly would hide.
whenOtherWins: 如果只是想快速预览题目范围，可以先粗看目录；真正训练输出能力时必须先独立作答。
tradeoff: 先自己产出暴露缺口 vs 先读答案获得结构感

termDefinitions.meaning: 面试开始时明确的功能性和非功能性需求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Requirements are the functional and non-functional constraints you clarify at the start.

termDefinitions.meaning: 官方参考题解，用来对照自己的设计差距。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An answer key is the reference solution used to compare against your own design.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用来画架构图的绘图工具或表面。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A whiteboard is a drawing surface used to sketch the architecture.

optionExplanations: 直接背下答案文本，记住的是别人的结构，不是你自己的判断，面试现场用不上。
先按需求独立设计一版，把 answer key 留到最后当对照，才能看清自己真正漏了哪条需求或哪个深潜。
读到一半就借着答案的思路往下写，后半段其实是被牵着走，测不出自己的真实缺口。
看着架构图照抄，省下的是自己组织架构这一步，练到的只是临摹。
optionExplanations_en: Memorizing the answer key's text copies someone else's structure, not your own judgment, and it won't hold up live.
Design your own version against the requirements first and save the answer key for comparison — that's what actually reveals your real gaps.
Reading halfway through and finishing off with the answer's logic means the second half isn't really yours, so it hides your real gaps.
Copying straight from the diagram skips the step of organizing the architecture yourself — you only practice tracing.

scenario: 面试是远程共享白板的 45 分钟，你要边画边讲，自己练习时想还原这个形式。
scenario_en: The interview is 45 minutes on a shared remote whiteboard where you draw while you talk, and you want practice to match that.
q: 自己练习系统设计题时可以使用什么工具或形式？
q_en: What tool or format should you use when practicing a design question by yourself?
options: 全程只在脑子里默想，不写也不画出来
只写出最终的数据库 schema，跳过前面过程
用 Guided Practice 或虚拟白板动手练
只死记硬背一份组件名称清单
options_en: Only think it through mentally the whole time, without writing or drawing anything.
Only write out the final database schema and skip everything that comes before it.
Use Guided Practice or a virtual whiteboard to work through it hands-on.
Only rote-memorize a single list of component names.
why: 系统设计要练结构化输出和图上表达；白板练习逼你把需求、组件、数据流和深潜显式画出来。
why_en: Guided practice or a virtual whiteboard forces you to make requirements, components, and data flow explicit instead of staying in your head.

termDefinitions.meaning: HelloInterview 提供的分步骤引导式练习工具，边做边给反馈。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Guided Practice is a step-by-step exercise tool that gives feedback as you design.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一款免费的在线虚拟白板绘图工具。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Excalidraw is a free online virtual whiteboard drawing tool.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据库表结构的定义。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A schema is the defined structure of a database's tables.

optionExplanations: 全程只在脑子里想，面试官看不到思考过程，这一步等于没练。
只写最终 schema 跳过了权衡取舍的展示，缺了需求和组件流这些环节。
用 Guided Practice 或白板动手练，能强迫自己把需求、组件、数据流显式画出来讲清楚。
背组件名单不等于会把它们放进架构里做判断，两者是不同能力。
optionExplanations_en: Keeping it all in your head means an interviewer never sees your thought process — this practically skips the exercise.
Writing only the final schema skips showing your tradeoffs, missing requirements and component flow along the way.
Guided Practice or a whiteboard forces you to lay out requirements, components, and data flow explicitly, out loud.
Memorizing a list of component names isn't the same as placing them into an architecture and reasoning about it.

scenario: 你已经做过几道题，读题解时感觉能看懂，但还没有在计时压力下讲过完整设计。
scenario_en: You have practiced a few questions and can follow the write-ups, but you have not explained a full design under time pressure.
q: 下一步最应该做什么？
q_en: What should you do next?
options: 找目标公司或相近背景的工程师做 peer mock
继续只看书面题解，一直看到面试当天都不改变
感觉能看懂题解内容就够了，直接停止练习
只反复练习画架构图，全程都不开口讲话
options_en: Run a peer mock with someone from the target company or a similar background.
Keep reading write-ups only, all the way up to interview day, without changing anything.
Decide that understanding the write-up is enough and stop practicing entirely.
Only keep practicing the diagram over and over, never speaking out loud at all.
why: 系统设计是口头沟通的面试；在计时压力下讲出取舍、澄清和深潜，和安静读懂文章是两种不同能力。
why_en: Mock interviews train the spoken, time-constrained version of design that silent reading cannot replicate.
whenOtherWins: 如果基础概念还没建立，应先补 core concepts 和框架；过早 mock 只会暴露太多基础缺口。
tradeoff: 口头表达训练 vs 静态阅读理解

termDefinitions.meaning: 和另一位工程师模拟真实计时面试。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A peer mock is a timed practice interview run with another engineer.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统设计里可复用的基础概念。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Core concepts are the reusable system-design ideas used across designs.

optionExplanations: 已经能看懂题解但没在计时压力下讲过时，找懂目标公司风格的人做 peer mock，练的正是缺的那块表达。
继续只读文章补不上表达短板，这个场景缺的从来不是输入量。
看懂不等于讲得出，停在这一步会把口头表达的缺口带进真实面试。
只练画图不开口，跳过了面试官真正在评估的沟通和临场应变。
optionExplanations_en: Once you can follow write-ups but haven't spoken under time pressure, a peer mock with someone from the target company trains exactly that missing skill.
More reading won't close a speaking gap — input isn't what's missing in this scenario.
Understanding isn't the same as explaining out loud; stopping here carries that gap straight into the real interview.
Drawing without narrating skips the communication and live improvising an interviewer actually grades.

scenario: 你刚开始练 system design，想选择第一批题来建立信心和基本套路。
scenario_en: You are just starting system design practice and want your first problems to build confidence and basic patterns.
q: 更合理的选择是什么？
q_en: Which starting point is more reasonable?
options: 直接从 Google Docs、Payment System、ChatGPT 开始
从 Bitly、Dropbox、News Aggregator 等 easy 题开始
只看 More Practice 里没有 write-up 的题
不选题，直接做 mock
options_en: Jump straight into Google Docs, Payment System, and ChatGPT.
Start with easy problems such as Bitly, Dropbox, and News Aggregator.
Only use More Practice problems that have no write-up.
Skip picking a problem and go straight to a mock.
why: 新手先用 easy 题训练框架和基本组件选择，再逐步上 medium/hard；过早做 hard 题容易误判为“系统设计太难”。
why_en: Beginners should start with easy problems to build the delivery framework before moving into harder designs.
whenOtherWins: 如果你已有大量系统设计经验，可以直接用 medium/hard 题查漏补缺。
tradeoff: 先易后难打基础 vs 直接挑战高难度题

termDefinitions.meaning: 题目附带的完整书面题解文章。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A write-up is the full written solution article that comes with a question.

termDefinitions.meaning: 和另一人模拟真实计时面试。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A mock is a timed practice interview with another person.

optionExplanations: 新手一上来就啃 Google Docs、Payment System 这类难题，框架不熟又要扛复杂约束，两头都学不会。
从 Bitly、Dropbox 这类 easy 题起步，能在可控复杂度下把框架用顺，再逐步叠加难度。
没有 write-up 对照，新手很难自己发现漏了哪条需求或哪个深潜。
没练过框架就直接上 mock，现场会漏步骤、讲不完整。
optionExplanations_en: Starting on hard problems like Google Docs or Payment System stacks an unfamiliar framework on heavy constraints at once.
Starting with easy problems like Bitly or Dropbox lets you get comfortable with the framework before adding difficulty.
Without a write-up to compare against, beginners struggle to spot which requirement or deep dive they missed.
Jumping to a mock without framework practice means missing steps and an incomplete answer live.

scenario: 你在 HelloInterview 的题单里发现，一部分题在正文 common questions，另一部分只出现在 More Practice 区。
scenario_en: In the HelloInterview question list, some problems are in common questions, while others only appear in the More Practice section.
q: Common questions 表和 More Practice 表的主要区别是什么？
q_en: What is the main difference between Common questions and More Practice?
options: More Practice 里的题全部是 easy 难度
Common questions 完全不能用来练习
只有 Common questions 附带 write-up
两个题单在内容和形式上完全没有差别
options_en: Every problem in More Practice is easy difficulty.
Common questions cannot be used for practice at all.
Only common questions come with a write-up.
The two lists have no difference in content or format.
why: 正文题单带书面题解，是主线练习材料；More Practice 是补充题库，强调引导练习和 AI 反馈，不一定有完整文章。
why_en: Common questions include a written guide, while More Practice adds extra guided problems that may not have a full write-up.
tradeoff: 带书面题解的主线材料 vs 靠引导反馈的补充题库

termDefinitions.meaning: 题目附带的完整书面题解文章。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A write-up is the full written solution article that comes with a question.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分步骤引导、边做边给反馈的练习工具。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Guided practice is a step-by-step exercise tool that gives feedback as you design.

termDefinitions.meaning: 练习过程中由 AI 即时给出的评价和建议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AI feedback is real-time evaluation and suggestions generated during practice.

optionExplanations: 两个题单其实都横跨 easy 到 hard，难度不是它们的区别点。
Common questions 一样能拿来练，区别只在于 More Practice 没有配套的书面文章。
只有正文题单额外配一篇完整 write-up，这决定你是先读文章复盘，还是直接上手引导练习。
两者在“是否带书面题解”上明显不同，混用学习方式会踩坑。
optionExplanations_en: Both lists actually span easy through hard — difficulty isn't what separates them.
Common questions are just as practicable; the gap is that More Practice ships without a companion article.
Only the main list adds a full write-up, which decides whether you read first or jump straight into guided practice.
The two clearly differ in whether a write-up exists, so treating them the same leads to the wrong study mode.

scenario: 你已经能独立完成 Bitly 和 Dropbox，但 medium 题会卡在深潜和 tradeoff。
scenario_en: You can complete Bitly and Dropbox on your own, but medium problems still trip you up on deep dives and tradeoffs.
q: 下一步最合理的练习目标是什么？
q_en: What is the most reasonable next practice target?
options: 换 Ticketmaster、Tinder 这类 medium 题练深潜
回头重新只看 intro 入门介绍文章
跳过 medium，直接冲 ChatGPT 这类 hard 题
感觉太难，直接停止刷题练习
options_en: Move to medium problems like Ticketmaster and Tinder to practice deep dives.
Go back to only reading the intro article.
Skip medium and jump straight to a hard problem like ChatGPT.
Feel discouraged and stop practicing altogether.
why: 难度要逐步递进：easy 建框架，medium 练真实 tradeoff，hard 再练复杂约束。
why_en: A good progression moves from easy framework practice into medium tradeoffs before tackling hard production complexity.
whenOtherWins: 如果连 easy 题都讲不完整，应先继续打磨框架，而不是急着升级难度。
tradeoff: 循序渐进升级难度 vs 跳级挑战更难的题

termDefinitions.meaning: 针对某个组件或场景做更细的设计展开。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A deep dive is a detailed exploration of one component or scenario in the design.

termDefinitions.meaning: 两个方案之间必须取舍的对比关系。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A tradeoff is the balance you strike when a choice benefits one thing at the cost of another.

optionExplanations: 已经能独立完成 easy 题、卡在深潜和 tradeoff 时，换 Ticketmaster、Tinder 这类 medium 题正好对上这个缺口。
框架已经会了，回头重看 intro 补不上深潜和 tradeoff 这块新缺口。
深潜的缺口还没补，直接冲 hard 题只会叠加更多复杂约束。
把卡壳当成停止的理由，缺口就永远没机会补上。
optionExplanations_en: Once easy problems are solid but deep dives and tradeoffs still trip you up, medium problems like Ticketmaster or Tinder target exactly that gap.
You already know the framework, so re-reading the intro won't fix a deep-dive or tradeoff gap.
The deep-dive gap is still open, so jumping to hard problems just stacks more constraints on top of it.
Treating getting stuck as a reason to quit means the gap never gets a chance to close.

q: 补全练习系统设计题的关键规则：
q_en: Fill in the key rule for practicing system design questions:
text: 先{{自己尝试}}，再看{{answer key}}；最后通过{{peer mock}}训练在时间压力下讲出设计。
why: 这条规则把输入学习变成输出训练：先产出，再对照，最后计时讲出来，三步都不能跳。
why_en: The rule turns passive input into active output: attempt first, compare against the answer, then rehearse it under time pressure.
tradeoff: 先产出后对照 vs 先看答案后模仿

termDefinitions.meaning: 官方参考题解，用来对照自己的设计差距。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An answer key is the reference solution used to compare against your own design.

termDefinitions.meaning: 和另一位工程师模拟真实计时面试。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A peer mock is a timed practice interview run with another engineer.

scenario: 你把某道题的 answer key 从头读到尾，觉得完全看懂了，但没有自己动手画过。
scenario_en: You read a question's answer key end to end and feel you understand it, but you have not drawn the design yourself.
q: 只看题解、不自己画设计，最容易造成什么问题？
q_en: What problem does reading the solution without drawing your own design most often cause?
options: 自动获得口头表达能力
自动知道所有 tradeoff
面试时完全不需要澄清需求
产生“看懂了”等于“会讲会设计”的错觉
options_en: You automatically gain verbal explanation skills.
You automatically know every tradeoff involved.
You no longer need to clarify requirements in the interview.
You get the illusion that understanding equals being able to design and explain it.
why: 阅读答案时结构和取舍已经被作者组织好了；面试现场你必须自己组织，这是两种不同能力。
why_en: Reading a solution can create a false sense of mastery because the author already organized the structure and tradeoffs for you.

termDefinitions.meaning: 官方参考题解，用来对照自己的设计差距。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An answer key is the reference solution used to compare against your own design.

optionExplanations: 口头表达要靠开口讲才能练出来，光读文章练不到这块。
换个约束取舍就会变，阅读一次记不住所有变体，谈不上自动掌握。
澄清需求是主动提问的技能，读答案完全不涉及这一步。
读答案时早已经有人替你把逻辑理顺了，你会误以为自己也能同样顺畅地讲出来、设计出来。
optionExplanations_en: Speaking skill only grows from speaking out loud — reading an article never trains it.
Change one constraint and the tradeoff changes with it; a single read can't cover every variant.
Clarifying requirements is an active questioning skill that reading the answer never exercises.
Someone else already smoothed out the logic for you while you read, so it's easy to mistake that for being able to explain or design it just as smoothly yourself.

scenario: 你练题时经常一会儿讲数据库、一会儿讲缓存、一会儿又回到需求，最后时间不够。
scenario_en: When practicing, you keep jumping from database to cache back to requirements, and you run out of time.
q: 应该如何修正这个跳题问题？
q_en: How should you fix this topic-jumping problem?
options: 继续想到哪讲到哪，完全不用任何框架来控制
只画出最终的架构图，跳过前面所有阶段
固定用 delivery framework，按阶段控制范围
跳过 requirements 环节，直接从架构开始讲
options_en: Keep improvising, jumping topics with no framework controlling any of it.
Only draw the final architecture diagram and skip every stage before it.
Commit to a delivery framework and control scope stage by stage.
Skip the requirements stage entirely and start straight from the architecture.
why: 框架的价值就是让你线性推进、防止 scope creep；系统设计是逐步收敛问题，不是脑暴组件。
why_en: A delivery framework keeps your answer linear and prevents scope creep during a fast-paced interview.
whenOtherWins: 如果你已经能自然组织答案，框架可以隐藏在表达里；但练习阶段仍应显式使用它。
tradeoff: 固定阶段推进 vs 想到哪讲到哪

termDefinitions.meaning: 面试时固定推进顺序的答题框架。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A delivery framework is a fixed sequence of stages for walking through a design answer.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面试开始时明确的功能性和非功能性需求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Requirements are the functional and non-functional constraints you clarify at the start.

optionExplanations: 跳题问题恰恰就是想到哪讲到哪造成的，继续这样只会让时间更不够用。
只画最终图跳过了前面阶段，架构图讲不清是怎么一步步推出来的。
固定用 delivery framework、按阶段设边界，正好把来回跳题这个问题从结构上消除。
跳过 requirements 直接讲架构，缺了需求锚点很容易整体设计跑偏。
optionExplanations_en: Improvising topic by topic is exactly what's causing the drift now — sticking with it just eats more time.
Jumping straight to the final diagram skips the earlier stages, so you can't justify how you got there.
Committing to a delivery framework and bounding each stage structurally removes the topic-jumping problem.
Skipping requirements and going straight to architecture removes the anchor that keeps the whole design on target.

scenario: 你已经刷了十道题，但每题都从零推导取舍，速度提不上来。
scenario_en: You have already drilled ten questions but still reason out every tradeoff from scratch, so you never get faster.
q: 先读 Core Concepts / Key Technologies / Patterns 的收益是什么？（多选）
q_en: What are the benefits of reading Core Concepts, Key Technologies, and Patterns first? (Select all that apply.)
options: 知道系统设计题常见组件和模式的边界
做题时能复用已有概念，而不是每题从零发明
帮助建立学习范围
保证不用再练任何题
options_en: You learn the boundaries of common components and patterns.
You can reuse existing concepts instead of reinventing them each time.
It helps you scope what you need to study.
It guarantees you never have to practice a question.
why: 基础材料不是替代练题，而是给练题提供词汇和取舍框架；没有基础，题解容易变成死记硬背。
why_en: The foundations give you reusable vocabulary and a tradeoff framework, but they do not replace active practice.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统设计里可复用的基础概念。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Core Concepts are the reusable system-design ideas used across designs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统设计常用的具体技术组件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Key Technologies are the concrete components used in designs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统设计里反复出现的架构套路。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Patterns are recurring architecture strategies seen across many designs.

optionExplanations: 知道常见组件和模式各自的适用边界，遇到新题能快速判断该往哪个方向想。
做题时能直接调用已学的概念当工具，省去每题重新发明轮子的时间。
明确该学多深多广，不会漫无目的地乱看资料。
读完基础不能替代输出训练，这个假设会让人误以为可以跳过练题。
optionExplanations_en: Knowing where common components and patterns apply lets you quickly judge which direction fits a new problem.
You can pull in concepts you've already learned as ready tools, saving you from reinventing them every time.
It clarifies how deep and broad to study, instead of wandering aimlessly through material.
Finishing the foundations never replaces output practice — assuming so wrongly suggests you can skip drilling problems.

scenario: 你已经练过几道题，准备进入 mock 阶段，想让反馈更贴近目标面试。
scenario_en: You have practiced several questions and are ready for mocks, but you want feedback that matches your target interview.
q: peer mock 对象怎么选更好？
q_en: Who is the better person to choose for a peer mock?
options: 只找完全不了解 system design 的人
优先找目标公司或相近风格的工程师
只对着镜子读答案
只用随机题目生成器，不要反馈
options_en: Find someone with no system design background at all.
Prioritize an engineer from the target company or a similar interview style.
Just read the answer out loud to a mirror.
Use a random question generator with no feedback.
why: 目标公司员工更熟悉该公司的面试节奏和评价偏好；反馈越贴近目标环境，练习价值越高。
why_en: A peer from the target company is more likely to give feedback aligned with that company's interview style.
whenOtherWins: 找不到目标公司的人时，找有系统设计面试经验的工程师，重点是拿到真实追问。
tradeoff: 贴近目标公司的真实反馈 vs 容易约到的泛泛反馈

termDefinitions.meaning: 和另一位工程师模拟真实计时面试。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A peer mock is a timed practice interview run with another engineer.

optionExplanations: 对方没有相关背景，提不出有价值的技术追问，反馈质量会很弱。
找目标公司或相近风格的工程师，追问方式和评分口味更接近真实面试官，反馈价值最高。
对镜子自读没有外部视角，漏掉的需求或取舍不会有人指出来。
只刷题不要反馈，等于主动放弃发现自己盲点的机会。
optionExplanations_en: Someone with no relevant background can't ask technically meaningful follow-ups, so the feedback stays weak.
An engineer from the target company or a similar style probes and grades closer to the real interviewer, which is why it's the highest-value pick.
Reading to a mirror gives no outside perspective, so no one flags the requirement or tradeoff you missed.
Drilling volume without feedback means deliberately giving up the chance to find your own blind spots.

scenario: 你读完二十篇题解，但真实面试要在 45 分钟里被追问着自己组织结构。
scenario_en: You have read twenty write-ups, but the real interview makes you organize the structure yourself in 45 minutes under follow-ups.
q: “读懂题解”和“面试中讲出设计”的最大区别是什么？
q_en: What is the biggest difference between understanding a write-up and explaining a design in an interview?
options: 讲出设计要在时间压力下自己组织结构和取舍
读懂题解更难，因为不需要表达
两者完全一样
讲出设计不需要任何技术判断
options_en: Explaining a design out loud means organizing structure and tradeoffs yourself, under time pressure.
Reading a write-up is harder because it requires no explanation.
The two are exactly the same skill.
Explaining a design requires no technical judgment at all.
why: 面试是实时沟通：要澄清需求、排序问题、画图、解释取舍并响应追问；阅读只是输入的一部分。
why_en: Speaking a design out loud requires actively organizing structure, tradeoffs, and communication under time pressure.
tradeoff: 主动组织表达 vs 被动接收阅读
optionExplanations: 面试官真正评估的是能不能在限时下自己组织结构、取舍并回应追问，这正是讲和读的分水岭。
现实是讲出来通常比读懂更难，这个说法把难度关系反过来了。
把两者当同一件事，会让人误以为看懂题解就等于能上场面试。
系统设计全程都在考技术判断，讲设计恰恰离不开它，不是剥离掉它。
optionExplanations_en: What interviewers actually grade is whether you can organize structure and tradeoffs yourself under time pressure and handle follow-ups — that's the real dividing line.
In reality speaking is usually harder than reading, so this reverses the actual difficulty.
Treating them as identical wrongly implies that understanding a write-up means you're ready to interview.
Technical judgment is exactly what's being tested throughout — explaining a design can't strip it out.

scenario: 主线 common questions 题单大约有 30 道，分布在 easy（约 4 道）、medium（约 13 道）、hard（约 13 道）三档。
scenario_en: The main common questions list has about 30 problems across easy, medium, and hard tiers: roughly 4 easy, 13 medium, and 13 hard.
q: 这个题量和难度分布，最支持哪条备考策略？
q_en: What prep strategy does this problem count and difficulty split support?
options: 跳过 medium，直接从 easy 冲到 hard
题量太少，应该把每道题都刷三遍以上
只刷 hard，因为面试通常只考最难的题
在三档难度里都抽样练习，而不是只刷一档
options_en: Skip medium and jump straight from easy to hard.
The list is so small you should redo every problem three times.
Only drill hard problems, since interviews are usually the hardest.
Sample practice across all three difficulty tiers instead of only one.
why: 约 30 道题里 easy 只有约 4 道、medium 和 hard 各约 13 道，难度偏中高；两周内做不完全部，应在三档里都抽样练习，覆盖面试可能出现的各种难度，而不是只啃一档或反复刷同一批题。
why_en: About thirty problems, only ~4 easy but ~13 medium and ~13 hard, so the spread leans harder; in a short window sample across all three tiers for coverage rather than drilling only one.

termDefinitions.meaning: 文章正文列出的主线练习题单，带书面 write-up。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Common questions are the main practice list in the article, each with a written guide.

optionExplanations: 跳过 medium 直接冲 hard，会跳过题量最大的 medium 这一档（约 13 道），练习覆盖不到面试最常出现的难度区间。
两周根本刷不完同一批题三遍，时间全耗在重复上，反而挤掉了拓宽覆盖面的机会。
面试并不是只考最难的题，easy 和 medium 合起来占了大半题量，只刷 hard 会漏掉大多数常见难度。
面试可能出到任何一档，在 easy/medium/hard 三档里都抽样练习，才覆盖得到实际会遇到的难度，而不是把时间压在单一一档上。
optionExplanations_en: Skipping medium and rushing straight to hard misses the largest tier, the ~13 medium problems, leaving the most common difficulty range uncovered.
You can't get through the same batch three times in two weeks anyway; the repetition just eats the time you'd use to broaden coverage.
Interviews aren't only the hardest tier; easy and medium together make up most of the list, so drilling only hard misses most of the common range.
An interview can land on any tier, so sampling across easy, medium, and hard covers the real difficulty range instead of over-investing in a single one.

scenario: 你独立完成一题后，对比 answer key 发现自己的高层架构不同。
scenario_en: After completing a problem independently, you compare with the answer key and find that your high-level architecture is different.
q: 最有价值的复盘方式是什么？
q_en: What is the most useful way to review the difference?
options: 把自己已经写好的完整答案直接删除掉，然后从头重新再做一遍
只核对两边设计里用的组件名称是否完全一致，不看别的东西
跳过复盘这个环节，直接跳到下一道新的练习题目上
比较双方背后的 requirements 和 tradeoffs
options_en: Delete the complete answer you already wrote and start over again from scratch.
Only check whether the component names on both sides match exactly, and look at nothing else.
Skip the review step entirely and jump straight to a brand-new practice question.
Compare the requirements and tradeoffs behind the difference.
why: 系统设计通常没有唯一图；复盘要找出作者为什么选了某个组件、你漏了哪个约束、哪些取舍没讲清。
why_en: The useful review compares requirements and tradeoffs behind the difference, not the memorization of one architecture diagram.
whenOtherWins: 如果你的方案违反了硬性需求或指标，那不是风格差异，是需要修正的设计错误。
diagram:
flowchart LR
    Mine["My design"] --> Gap["Find gaps"]
    Key["Answer key"] --> Gap
    Gap --> Req["Requirements"]
    Gap --> Trade["Tradeoffs"]
    Gap --> Deep["Deep dives"]
tradeoff: 复盘约束和取舍 vs 复盘表面架构图

termDefinitions.meaning: 官方参考题解，用来对照自己的设计差距。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An answer key is the reference solution used to compare against your own design.

termDefinitions.meaning: 设计必须满足的硬性限制条件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Constraints are the hard limits a design must satisfy.

termDefinitions.meaning: 两个方案之间必须取舍的对比关系。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Tradeoffs are the balances you strike when a choice benefits one thing at the cost of another.

optionExplanations: 架构不同不等于方案失败，直接删除重做会丢掉本可以拿来对比学习的素材。
只核对组件名称是否一致，看不出背后的决策逻辑，组件名一样理由也可能完全不同。
跳过复盘等于放弃这道题给的反馈，同样的缺口会在下一题重复出现。
架构不同时去比较双方的 requirements 和 tradeoffs，才能定位自己漏掉的约束或没考虑到的取舍。
optionExplanations_en: A different architecture isn't failure — deleting and redoing from scratch throws away material you could learn from by comparing.
Matching component names alone hides the reasoning behind them; identical names can still come from very different logic.
Skipping the review gives up the feedback this problem offers, and the same gap will resurface on the next one.
Comparing the requirements and tradeoffs behind a different architecture is what actually pinpoints the constraint or tradeoff you missed.

q: 补全准备路线的三个基础动作：
q_en: Fill in the three foundation steps in the preparation path:
text: 理解{{system design interview}}是什么，选择{{Delivery Framework}}，再学习{{Core Concepts}}、{{Key Technologies}}和{{Common Patterns}}。
why: 三步构成从面试形态到表达框架、再到知识地图的基础路线；缺一步，后面练习容易失焦。
why_en: The foundation is understanding the interview format, choosing a delivery framework, and then filling in core concepts, technologies, and patterns.
tradeoff: 先搭完整基础 vs 边练边补概念

termDefinitions.meaning: 面试时固定推进顺序的答题框架。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Delivery Framework is a fixed sequence of stages for walking through a design answer.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统设计里可复用的基础概念。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Core Concepts are the reusable system-design ideas used across designs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统设计常用的具体技术组件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Key Technologies are the concrete components used in designs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统设计里反复出现的架构套路。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Common Patterns are recurring architecture strategies seen across many designs.

scenario: 你没有练习伙伴，但想先自己模拟白板设计流程。
scenario_en: You do not have a practice partner yet, but you want to simulate the whiteboard design flow by yourself.
q: 没有练习伙伴时，可行替代是什么？
q_en: What is a workable substitute before you have a mock partner?
options: 什么都不做，只是干等 mock 搭子出现
只截图收藏别人写好的完整答案，不自己动手
用 Guided Practice 或白板自己讲一遍
只写代码，完全跳过画架构图这一步
options_en: Do nothing at all and just wait around for a mock partner to show up.
Only screenshot and collect other people's complete answers, without doing any work yourself.
Use Guided Practice or a whiteboard to narrate it yourself.
Only write code and skip the step of drawing an architecture diagram entirely.
why: 没有 peer 时也能用 guided practice 或白板练结构化输出；重点是不要停留在只读的模式。
why_en: Guided practice or a virtual whiteboard lets you practice structured output even before you find a mock partner.
whenOtherWins: 能独立讲完整后，仍应尽快找 mock，因为真实追问很难自我模拟。
tradeoff: 自己动手画讲 vs 被动等待搭子

termDefinitions.meaning: HelloInterview 提供的分步骤引导式练习工具，边做边给反馈。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Guided Practice is a step-by-step exercise tool that gives feedback as you design.

termDefinitions.meaning: 和另一人模拟真实计时面试。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A mock is a timed practice interview with another person.

optionExplanations: 干等搭子出现，等待的这段时间完全练不到任何东西。
截图收藏别人的答案不会训练你自己的表达或设计能力，跟没练一样。
没有搭子时用 Guided Practice 或白板自己边画边讲，照样能练到结构化输出这一步。
只写代码跳过架构图，漏掉了需求、组件和取舍这几个真正要练的环节。
optionExplanations_en: Waiting around for a partner to show up produces zero practice volume in the meantime.
Screenshotting and saving other people's answers trains neither your explanation nor your design skill — it's the same as not practicing.
Without a partner, narrating your own design with Guided Practice or a whiteboard still trains structured output.
Writing only code and skipping the diagram misses the requirements, components, and tradeoffs that actually need practice.

scenario: 你在练题时没有固定推进顺序，想到哪讲到哪。
scenario_en: When practicing, you have no fixed answer order and just say whatever comes to mind.
q: 没有清晰 roadmap 的系统设计回答最容易出现什么问题？
q_en: What problem does a system design answer without a clear roadmap most often run into?
options: 所有问题都会自动收敛，完全不用管它
已经不再需要澄清任何需求，可以跳过
即兴发挥的效果必然比用框架更快更好
scope creep：不断发散、偏离核心需求
options_en: All problems will automatically converge on their own, no effort needed at all.
You no longer need to clarify any requirements, so that step can be skipped.
Improvising is guaranteed to work out faster and better than using a framework.
Scope creep: the discussion keeps drifting away from core requirements.
why: 面试时间有限，发散会吃掉高层设计和关键深潜的时间；框架的作用就是让你知道下一步该讲什么。
why_en: Without a roadmap, answers tend to drift into scope creep and lose time needed for the core design.

termDefinitions.meaning: 讨论不断扩散、偏离核心需求的现象。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Scope creep is when the discussion keeps expanding beyond the core requirements.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面试回答时预先规划好的阶段顺序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A roadmap is the pre-planned sequence of stages for answering the interview.

optionExplanations: 现实恰恰相反，没有框架讨论更容易发散，不会自动收敛。
没有 roadmap 不等于不用澄清需求，跳过这步反而更容易让设计整体跑偏。
即兴发挥来回摸索方向，实际比按框架推进更费时间，不是更快。
没有 roadmap 时讨论会不断发散、偏离核心需求，高层设计和深潜的时间就被无关话题占用了。
optionExplanations_en: In reality the opposite happens — without a framework, discussions drift instead of converging on their own.
No roadmap doesn't mean skipping clarification; skipping it actually makes the whole design more likely to drift off target.
Improvising and backtracking usually costs more time than following a framework, not less.
Without a roadmap, discussion keeps expanding away from core requirements, eating the time meant for high-level design and deep dives.

scenario: 你只有两周准备系统设计，基础薄弱，但每天能练习。
scenario_en: You have only two weeks to prepare for system design, your foundation is weak, but you can practice every day.
q: 最合理的时间分配倾向是什么？
q_en: What time-allocation strategy makes the most sense?
options: 快速过一遍基础，再用 easy/medium 题主动输出
两周时间全部拿来看书面题解，完全不做任何输出练习
只做 hard 难度的题目，完全不补任何基础概念
只死记硬背一整份系统设计技术名词列表
options_en: Skim the foundations fast, then drill active output on easy/medium problems.
Spend the entire two weeks only reading write-ups, with no output practice at all.
Only work on hard-difficulty problems, without filling in any foundational concepts.
Only rote-memorize one entire list of system design terminology.
why: 短期备考要先建最低可用框架，再尽快进入输出练习；短板通常在讲题过程中才暴露。
why_en: With limited time, build the minimum framework quickly and spend most effort on active easy-to-medium practice.
whenOtherWins: 如果基础已经扎实，可以把更多时间投入 hard 题 mock 和深潜复盘。
tradeoff: 快速搭框架转向输出 vs 长时间只做输入阅读

termDefinitions.meaning: 面试时固定推进顺序的答题框架。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A delivery framework is a fixed sequence of stages for walking through a design answer.

optionExplanations: 两周时间紧、基础薄弱时，先快速过一遍基础再转向 easy/medium 输出练习，能同时补上概念缺口和表达短板。
两周全花在阅读上，面试现场才会暴露的表达短板完全没机会被发现。
基础还不牢就直接冲 hard 题，复杂约束会把人卡在半路。
背下名词列表不等于会用它们做设计判断，两周时间这样花性价比很低。
optionExplanations_en: With two weeks and weak basics, skim the foundations fast then shift into easy/medium output practice, closing both the concept gap and the speaking gap.
Spending the whole two weeks reading never exposes the speaking weakness that only shows up when you actually explain a design.
Rushing into hard problems before the basics are solid means heavy constraints stall you partway through.
Memorizing a list of terms isn't the same as using them to make design calls — a poor use of two weeks.

q: 按正确顺序排列一条完整的准备路线：
q_en: Put the full preparation path in the right order:
steps: 做 peer mock，训练在时间压力下沟通
理解面试形式并选择 delivery framework
从题单选择 easy/medium 题，先自己做再看答案
why: 完整路线是先知道怎么答，再补概念词汇，然后靠做题输出，最后用 mock 逼近真实面试。
why_en: The full path is understanding the format and framework, filling in the foundations, practicing problems actively, and finishing with mock interviews.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    I["Interview shape"] --> F["Framework"]
    F --> B["Basics"]
    B --> P["Easy/medium practice"]
    P --> M["Mock"]
tradeoff: 先搭路线图再逐步深入 vs 直接从做题开始

termDefinitions.meaningEn: A peer mock is a timed practice interview run with another engineer.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: Core Concepts are the reusable system-design ideas used across designs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统设计常用的具体技术组件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Key Technologies are the concrete components used in designs.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: Common Patterns are recurring architecture strategies seen across many designs.
